title: Finite counit normalization of clopen system transport
statement: For a purity datum [def-pur-conventions], a compactification [def-weil-compactifications-refinements] of a quasi-compact morphism [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] and an open and closed component [def-weil-open-immersion] [def-weil-closed-immersion], fix canonical clopen system core and transport-map data [def-pur-clopen-system-realization-data]. Define its finite-realization data to consist, at every positive coefficient exponent, of bounded-below witnesses for the actual exceptional values on bounded constructible inputs, the canonical open-insertion adjunction, and a natural finite exceptional restriction isomorphism satisfying the specified counit equation [lem-pur-clopen-counit-adjoint-comparison]. Include evaluation comparisons for the transported exceptional functors and restriction, identifying the evaluation of the already constructed system map with that finite counit-normalized map on constructible inputs. All finite operations are the existing intrinsic operations and all compactifications retain the same proper factor. This is a data type, without an assertion of existence. Use scalar-unit coordinate and evaluated-level comparisons [def-pur-adic-proetale-realization]. Use canonical site realization [def-pur-adic-derived-site-realization]. Use the compact-support adjunction mate [def-pur-adic-support-realization]. Use canonical finite pullback presentation [def-pur-pullback-reduction-realization]. Use the recorded canonical finite evaluation [def-pur-clopen-canonical-finite-evaluation]. Use the recorded canonical restriction evaluation [def-pur-clopen-canonical-restriction-evaluation]. The normalized restriction-evaluation data are [def-pur-clopen-restriction-evaluation-data].
